summary: The prose in all three docs (setOutDirect/setErrDirect/setInDirect) is accurate about direct-vs-restoring semantics, but each @param tag is phrased backwards/circularly, describing the parameter as "returned by" the getter of the same name instead of describing the parameter itself, and is inconsistent with the plain @param phrasing ("the new output stream.") used for the sibling `withOut`/`withErr`/`withIn` methods a few lines below in the same file.

items.issue: `@param out the new output stream returned by \`out\`` is circular/backwards: it reads as if the argument should be obtained from calling the `out` getter, when actually the reverse holds — after calling `setOutDirect`, the getter `out` will subsequently return whatever stream is passed in. A reader skimming just the @param line can plausibly misread the direction.
items.suggestion: Describe the parameter directly, e.g. "the new output stream to install as the default", matching the plain style used at line 182 (`@param out the new output stream.`).

items.issue: Same circular/backwards construction as setOutDirect's @param: `@param err the new error stream returned by \`err\`` implies the value comes from the `err` getter rather than stating that the getter will return it afterward.
items.suggestion: Use plain phrasing consistent with line 213/227's `@param err the new error stream.`

items.issue: Same circular/backwards construction: `@param in the new input reader returned by \`in\`` implies the value comes from the `in` getter rather than stating that the getter will return it afterward.
items.suggestion: Use plain phrasing consistent with `withIn`'s `@param reader the new input reader to use as the default input source` (line 249).
